question: ap1
prompt:
Each of your ideas must draw on a domain unrelated to the research question below, for example through an analogy, a structure, a principle, or a pattern borrowed from that domain, while still being a concrete, scientifically sound way to address the question.

Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Flip-flop test with inducible AP-1 switch (electronics latch analogy)
ideas.description: Borrowing from an SR latch in electronics, which holds its state after the input pulse ends, use an optogenetic or degron-based system to pulse AP-1 (e.g., Fos/Jun) activity briefly, then withdraw it and track ATAC-seq, CUT&RUN for AP-1 and H3K27ac, and target-gene transcription over days. Memory is supported only if the chromatin and transcriptional state persist without ongoing AP-1 input, and the persistence should disappear when AP-1 binding sites are mutated.

ideas.title: Savings paradigm: faster re-induction after rest (relearning-curve analogy)
ideas.description: Following Ebbinghaus-style savings experiments in psychology, stimulate cells with a first exposure, rest them, then re-stimulate and compare the speed, amplitude, and magnitude of AP-1 target induction (time-resolved RNA-seq or live Fos/Jun reporters) against naive cells. A savings effect that vanishes in cells lacking AP-1 or with binding-site mutations would support a memory role specifically for AP-1.

ideas.title: Dendrochronology-style recorder for past AP-1 activity
ideas.description: Like tree rings that record past growing seasons, use a stable recorder such as an inducible CreER or a slow-maturing fluorescent timer under an AP-1 responsive promoter to permanently mark cells that had AP-1 activity at a defined time. Then measure, by flow or imaging, whether marked cells respond differently to a later stimulus and whether the mark is retained across divisions and after AP-1 withdrawal.

ideas.title: Serial-passage propagation test (sourdough starter analogy)
ideas.description: A sourdough starter keeps its character only by being transferred serially, so test whether AP-1-induced states are carried forward the same way: stimulate a culture, then passage cells through many divisions without stimulus, sampling at intervals for chromatin accessibility and transcription at AP-1 targets. Persistence across passages, measured against lineage-matched controls and AP-1 knockouts, would indicate heritable memory rather than a transient response.

ideas.title: Mitotic bookmarking dissection with degron-based AP-1 removal
ideas.description: Drawing on the idea of a bookmark that survives a page turn, synchronize cells, remove AP-1 specifically in mitosis or G1 using a degron, and measure whether AP-1-bound enhancers keep accessibility and H3K27ac through mitosis and into daughter cells. Comparing retention with versus without AP-1 binding and with dCas9 site-specific mutants would separate active memory maintenance from passive chromatin persistence.
